description: Local Area Network discovery tool with an interactive Terminal User Interface (TUI) written in Go.  Discover, explore, and understand your LAN in an intuitive way. Knock Knock.. who's there? 🚪

summary.one_liner: A Go terminal UI tool that discovers and explores devices on your local network using unprivileged mDNS, SSDP, and ARP-cache scanning, with OUI manufacturer lookup.
summary.what_it_does: Whosthere runs unprivileged, concurrent discovery scans using mDNS and SSDP scanners. It also sweeps the local subnet by opening TCP/UDP connections to trigger ARP resolution, then reads the ARP cache to list devices. Discovered devices are enriched with OUI lookups to show manufacturers. The interactive TUI lets you navigate, regex-search, view device details, copy IP or MAC addresses, and run an optional port scan on a selected device. It also has a CLI mode that performs a single scan with optional JSON output, and a daemon mode that serves device data over a small HTTP API (/devices, /device/{ip}, /health). Devices can be given custom aliases, which can be bulk-imported or exported as YAML, and the look can be changed through themes and YAML configuration.
use_cases: Find out which devices are connected to my home network
Scan a LAN from the command line and output JSON
Run a background daemon that exposes discovered devices over HTTP
Name devices on my network with aliases imported from a YAML file
Check which services are open on devices I own
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd whosthere && make build
notable: Unprivileged discovery: populates the ARP cache via TCP/UDP connections, so no root or admin rights are needed
Combines mDNS, SSDP, and ARP-cache scanning with OUI manufacturer lookup
Interactive TUI with regex search, vim-style navigation, and runtime theme switching
Daemon mode with a simple HTTP API for integration with other tools
Alias import/export as YAML, with MAC address normalization across common formats
caveats: Clipboard copy needs an OS tool installed (pbcopy, clip.exe, xsel/xclip, or wl-copy), and it relies on a fork of go-clipboard
Unprivileged scanning may not be comprehensive; the README says it is not a professional-grade monitoring tool
Scanning large subnets (bigger than /16) sends a very large amount of traffic and requires enabling scan_large_subnets
Intended only for networks you have permission to scan
